is_hardcoded_string(value) {

    value.value != ""
    glitch_lib.traverse_var(value)
}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    attrs := glitch_lib.all_attributes(parent)
    attr := attrs[_]
    regex.match(credential_name_pattern, attr.name)

        "type": "sec_hard_secr",
        "element": attr,
        "path": parent.path,

    }
}

}

**What the rule was attempting to detect:**
The rule tries to identify hardcoded credentials (passwords, keys, tokens, usernames, etc.) in IaC files by matching attribute names, variable names, or hash keys against a credential-related regex pattern, then checking whether the associated value is a literal, non-empty, non-path string with no variable references.

The rule has no way to distinguish an LDAP user DN (a non-secret identity string) from an actual hardcoded secret—it treats any string value under a `user`-named key as a credential.
